That auspicious river Dhunī, known as Dhūtapāpā, embodies all sacred fords; she sweeps away masses of great sins just as trees growing on her banks are washed away.

At that time, when the celestial river (Svardhunī) was not present there at the sacred ford of Dharmatīrtha, which is endowed with the power to wash away sins, the Sun-god (Bradhna) performed his ascetic penance.
The Lord Gabhastimālī, in the presence of Gabhastīśvara, performed fierce penance while meditating upon Gaurī Maṅgalā.
While he who was named Mayūkhāditya was performing austerities at that sacred site, a great sweat issued forth from his rays due to extreme exhaustion.
From the rays [of the sun], a continuous stream of great sweat issued forth; from that, she became the meritorious river named Kiraṇā.
The river named Kiraṇā, when joined by the Dhūtapāpā, destroys the blinding darkness of great sins merely by the act of bathing.
In the beginning, there was the holy river of Dharma, mingled with Dhūtapāpā, by whom all sins were washed away and whose very self was made into a sacred bathing place for all.
Furthermore, the rays that have gathered there and are augmented by the sun—by the mere remembrance of whose name even great delusion goes to blindness. (12)
In that auspicious Dharmanada, the two rivers Kiranā and Dhūtapāpā flow toward Vārāṇasī with pure waters, removing all evil.
Then Bhāgīrathī arrived together with that son of Dilīpa; Bhāgīrathī, Yamunā, and Sarasvatī all came together.
Kiraṇā, Dhūtapāpā, Puṇyatoyā, Sarasvatī, Gaṅgā, and Yamunā—these are celebrated here as the five rivers.
Therefore, there is a sacred ford named Pañcanada, renowned throughout the three worlds; one who bathes there shall not again assume a body composed of the five elements.
At this confluence of the five rivers, which shatters the flood of worldly existence, one goes forth merely by bathing, having pierced through the pavilion of the cosmic egg.
There are many sacred fords here at Kāśī at every step, yet they are not equal even to a ten-millionth part of the Pañcanada Tīrtha. || 18 ||
Whatever fruit is obtained by one who has properly bathed at Prayāga during the month of Māgha, that same fruit is certainly attained in a single day at Pañcanada in Kāśī.
Having bathed at the Pañcanada tīrtha and performed the libations for the ancestors, one who worships Bindumādhava shall not be subject to birth again.
For as many sesame seeds as are offered to the ancestors in the water libation at the meritorious Pañcanada Tīrtha, for that many years shall their satisfaction endure.
Those by whom the Śrāddha rite was performed with faith at the auspicious Pañcanada Tīrtha—their ancestors were liberated, even those who had entered various wombs.
In the world of Yama, this verse is sung by the hosts of ancestors upon beholding the greatness of the Pañcanada region through the performance of the śrāddha rites.
"Perhaps someone from our lineage will come here, reach Pañcanada at Kāśī, and perform a śrāddha ceremony, by which we may be liberated. (24)
This verse was daily recited by the ancestors in the presence of Śrāddhadeva at Pañcanada in Kāśī. (25)
Whatever wealth is given there at the Pañcanada Tīrtha, there shall be no exhaustion of that merit even at the end of a kalpa.
Even a barren woman, having bathed for a year in the Pañcanada lake and having worshipped Maṅgalā Gaurī, will certainly give birth to a son.
By bathing one's chosen deity with the holy waters of the Pañcanada river, purified by a cloth, one obtains great fruit.
The drop of water from the Pañcanada has surpassed in weight even the one hundred and eight jars filled with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).
The purification that is proclaimed for drinking the five-strand broom-grass (pañcakūrca) is attained by drinking with faith even a single drop of the water of the Pañcanada.

Whatever fruit may be obtained from the final purificatory bath (avabhṛtha-snāna) of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices, that same fruit is increased a hundredfold by bathing in the waters of the Pañcanada.
The Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices may serve as means for attaining heaven; however, bathing in the Pañcanada for even two ghaṭikās until the end of one's life leads to liberation.
Even the consecration for the kingdom of heaven is not as highly esteemed by the virtuous as the consecration at Pañcanada, which bestows no small measure of happiness.
It is better for a servant to reach Vārāṇasī and perform the five river ablutions than to become a servant to ten million kings elsewhere, O Lord of Men. (34)
Those who have not bathed at Pañcanada during the sin-removing month of Kārttika remain in the womb even today; they shall dwell in the womb once again.
In the Kṛta age it is named Dharmanada; in Tretā, Dhūtapāpaka; in Dvāpara, Bindutīrtha; and in the Kali age, it is remembered as Pañcanada.
Whatever fruit is obtained by performing austerities for a hundred years in the Kṛta age, that is attained by bathing just once at Pañcanada during the month of Kārtika.

Whatever fruit may arise from other meritorious acts, such as sacrifices and charitable works performed throughout one's life, that same fruit shall be obtained by bathing in the Dharmanadī during the month of Kārttika. || 38 ||
O Dhūtapāpa, there is no sacred ford anywhere on the surface of the earth equal to this, by bathing in which even the sin accumulated over three lifetimes may be destroyed. (39)
Having given gold even the measure of a single *kṛṣṇala* at Bindutīrtha, a man shall never become poor, nor shall he ever be deprived of gold.
Having given cows, land, sesame seeds, gold, horses, garments, food, garlands, ornaments, or whatever else at Bindu-tīrtha here, one obtains that which is imperishable.
Having offered even a single oblation into a well-kindled fire according to the prescribed rite at the holy Dharmanada Tīrtha, one obtains the fruit of ten million burnt offerings (koṭihoma).
O abodes of the auspiciousness of the four goals of human life, no one is able to describe the infinite greatness of the Pañcanada Tīrtha. (43)
Having heard this meritorious narrative, or having caused it to be heard with devotion, one whose soul is purified of all sins is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.

Thus ends the fifty-ninth chapter, titled "The Manifestation of Pañcanada," in the latter half of the Kāśī-khaṇḍa, within the fourth section of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 59 ||
Skanda said: O son of Mitra and Varuṇa, the origin of Pañcanada has been told; now I shall describe the supreme manifestation of Mādhava.
Having heard this with faith, the wise person is instantly liberated from sins; he shall not be deprived of prosperity and shall be united with virtue.
Having come from Mount Mandara and having taken leave of the moon-crested Lord, Upendra, traveling in his chariot drawn by Tārkṣya, reached the city of Vārāṇasī in an instant.
Having eradicated Divodāsa, the protector of the earth, by means of his own illusory power, he remained at the Pādodaka Tīrtha in his true form as the one named Keśava.
Having thoroughly reflected upon the supreme greatness of Kāśī and having beheld the Pañcanada Tīrtha, he indeed attained the highest joy.
And the lotus-eyed one, with a gracious soul, said: "O Vaikuṇṭha, even your innumerable qualities have been enumerated by me."
Where in the Ocean of Milk are there so many pure virtues as those which are found here in Kāśī, in the Pañcanada pool? (7)
Even in Śvetadvīpa, where could such a preeminent collection of virtues be found as that which exists in Kāśī, the purifier that washes away sins?
Yet, O Mūḍha, the touch of the Kaumodakī does not produce in me that same effect as the contact with the water that washes away sins does in every way. || 9 ||
The pleasure I derive from embracing the Ocean-born Goddess with her limbs entwined is not such as it would be here, were she touched by one whose sins have been washed away.
Thus, at the Pañcanada tīrtha, the Consort of the Daughter of the Milk Ocean dispatched Tārkṣya to the presence of the Three-eyed Lord to report the news.
He described the collection of meritorious virtues arising from the Forest of Bliss (Ānandakānana), belonging to King Divodāsa, which originated in the land of Pañcanada.
Seated comfortably, joyful, and with a clear vision, Viṣṭaraśravas beheld the ascetic whose wealth was his penance, who was emaciated in limb yet enriched by austerity.
That sage, having approached the lotus-eyed Acyuta, who was seated upon a lotus and adorned with a forest garland; || 14 ||
His four shimmering hands hold the conch, lotus, mace, and discus; his chest is illuminated by the Kaustubha gem, and he is clothed in yellow silk garments.
He possesses the luster of a blue lotus, a most tender and sweet form, a lotus shining from his navel-lake, and very rosy lips.
He whose teeth were like pomegranate seeds, who illuminated the sky with his crown, whose feet were worshipped by Indra, and who was praised by Sanaka and the other sages.
Its great majesty was celebrated by divine sages such as Nārada and others, and its heart was gladdened by the devotees of the Lord, such as Prahlāda and others.
He who holds the staff-like bow Śārṅga, who has punished all the Dānavas, who is the slayer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and who signaled the destruction of Kaṃsa.
That which is absolute liberation, the Supreme Brahman, formless and beyond the reach of the senses—He has manifested in human form for the sake of the devotion of His devotees.
The Vedas did not know His form, nor was it revealed by the Upanishads; neither Brahmā nor the other gods made Him the guest of their eyes.
Filled with joy, that sage Agnibindu, a man of great asceticism, bowed down to Hṛṣīkeśa, placing his head upon the ground.
With his hands joined in añjali and placed upon his head, he praised Acyuta, the destroyer of Bali, who was seated upon a broad stone slab, with supreme devotion.
There, in the vicinity of the Pañcanada, frequented by Mārkaṇḍeya and others, Agnibindu, with a satisfied mind, praised Govinda.
Agnibindu said: Om, salutations to the lotus-eyed one, the bestower of purity both internal and external; the Puruṣa with a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet. (25)
I bow to Your pair of feet, O Viṣṇu, which ward off all dualities; with a mind free from duality, I salute You who are praised by the gods, such as Jiṣṇu and others.
Who here is able to praise Him whom even the words of Vācaspati cannot reach? Devotion alone is powerful in this matter. (27)
How can that Blessed One, the Lord who transcends speech and is beyond the range of the mind and its faculties, be praised by those like us of meager intellect? (28)
Who would have the power to praise Him whom speech does not enter as its object, nor whom the mind here can conceive, He who transcends both mind and speech? (29)
By whom can the great majesty of that God be comprehended, whose very breath is the Vedas with their six limbs and the methods of Pada and Krama?
Even Sanaka and the others, though they meditate with unwearied mind, intellect, and senses upon Him within the space of their hearts, do not find Him in His true nature.
Even his life-story, which is sung by the best of sages such as Nārada and others who have been celibates from childhood, cannot be fully comprehended.

Who knows you—subtle in form, unborn, undecaying, the one primordial source, beyond the reach of Brahmā and the other gods, unconquerable, possessed of infinite power, eternal, free from affliction, formless, yet possessing an inconceivable form; O you who are both the moving and the unmoving, and yet distinct from the moving and the unmoving?

O Murāri, each single instance of chanting your name—whether as Mukunda, Madhusūdana, or Mādhava—shall remove the great burden of sins accumulated over lifetimes by those who are sinful, and it shall bestow the highly honored fruit of a great sacrifice when thus recited.

"O Nārāyaṇa! O Savior from the ocean of hell! O Dāmodara! O Slayer of Madhu! O Four-armed One! O Sustainer of the Universe! O Viraja! O Janārdana!"—for those who chant these names here, where is there birth, and where is the fear of Death? (35)

O Trivikrama, those who always cultivate within their hearts you—the lotus-eyed one whose splendor is as beautiful as a bank of clouds, your form draped in a garment of flashing lightning—they too shall touch your inconceivable radiance.

O Lord marked with the Śrīvatsa, Hari, Acyuta, Slayer of Kaiṭabha, Govinda, whose chariot is Tārkṣya, Keśava, wielder of the discus; O Lord of Lakṣmī, Destroyer of the Danujas, wielder of the Śārṅga bow: for the man who possesses devotion to You, there is no fear anywhere.

O Blessed One, those of pure nature by whom You were worshipped with tulasī flowers—divine in fragrance and surpassing the scent of musk—those very ones all the hosts of gods in heaven worship profusely with garlands of mandāra flowers.

O lotus-eyed one, for those who have Your name—which grants all desires—on their speech; for those whose ears possess the sweet syllables of Your story; and for those upon the wall of whose hearts Your form is painted: for them, the state of being a king beyond all forms is not difficult to attain.

O Lord of Śrī, O Sovereign of the Ancestors, O Kubera and foremost of the gods, those who constantly worship you, who recline upon the earth, are always honored in heaven by the deities—you, who are skilled in bestowing a continuous stream of the happiness of both heaven and liberation.

O Lord with lotus-like eyes, those hosts of Siddhas, Apsaras, and gods who constantly praise You—praising the one who holds a radiant lotus in His hand—do not obtain the beautiful lotus of Nirvana, which bestows all perfections, without You.

You destroy, you protect, and you create the universe in an instant through Your own play, O You who assume playful forms and whose pair of feet are bowed to by Brahmā; You alone are the Supreme Lord of the universe, and You alone are the seed of the universe—I bow to You eternally.

O enemy of the lord of the Danujas, you alone are the praiser; you are the praise, and you alone are the one to be praised, for you alone exist as everything here. O Viṣṇu, I perceive nothing whatsoever as distinct from you; O enemy of worldly existence, forever quench my thirst born of this world.
Having thus praised Hṛṣīkeśa, Agnibindu, of great austerity, stood silent; thereupon Viṣṇu, the bestower of boons, spoke to the sage.
Śrī Viṣṇu said: "O Agnibindu, O highly wise one, O treasury of great austerities! Choose a boon; being well-pleased, there is nothing that should not be granted to you."
Agnibindu said: "O Blessed One, Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, Master of the Universe, Beloved of Kamalā, if you are pleased, then grant me that which I now pray for."
Then, having been granted permission by Hari with a movement of his eyebrows, that ascetic, having offered his salutation with a joyful heart, chose Keśava as his boon.
O Blessed One, stay here at the Pañcanada pool; for the welfare of all living beings, and especially for those seeking liberation.
O Lord of Lakṣmī, let this boon not be granted to me without due reflection; I desire no other boon than devotion at your lotus feet.
Having heard this boon from Agnibindu, Madhusūdana, the Lord of the Daughter of the Ocean, being pleased, said "So be it" for the sake of helping others.
Śrī Viṣṇu said: O Agnibindu, best of sages, I shall certainly remain here, pointing out the path to liberation for those men who possess devotion to Kāśī.
O Sage, I am pleased once again; choose a boon, for I shall grant it to you. You are exceedingly devoted to me, and may your devotion toward me remain firm.
"O treasure of asceticism, I indeed wish to remain right here from the very beginning; therefore, having been entreated by you, I shall certainly stay here forever. (53)
Having reached Kāśī, what person of dull intellect would abandon it, were he not lacking in wisdom? Having obtained a priceless ruby, who would desire a piece of glass? (54)
In this world, by means of very little exertion—merely through the exhaustion of the body—it is certain that one must quickly depart; for how else could liberation be attained? (55)
Having exchanged here this earthly body, worn out by old age, why indeed would the wise not accept the immortal, ageless form? (56)
Liberation is not obtained through austerities, nor by gifts, nor by sacrifices with abundant sacrificial fees; it is attained nowhere else as it is at Kāśī through the casting off of the body.
For even yogis who practice yoga with disciplined minds are not liberated in a single birth; rather, they are liberated in Kāśī through the casting off of the body.
This alone is the great gift, this alone is the great austerity, and this alone is the most excellent vow: that the body dies at Kāśī. 59.
He alone is truly wise in this world, he alone has conquered his senses, and he alone is meritorious and blessed who, having attained Kāśī, does not abandon it. (60)
O Sage, I shall remain here as long as Kāśī exists; for even at the time of universal dissolution, there is no destruction of this city, which is firmly established upon the tip of Śiva’s trident.
Having heard these words of Viṣṇu, the great sage Agnibindu, his hair standing on end with joy, spoke again: "I choose another boon."
O Lord of the Earth, by my name, at this auspicious Pañcanada Tīrtha, grant liberation always to all, both to the non-devotees and to the devotees.
Furthermore, grant liberation even to those men who, having bathed at Pañcanada and traveled to other lands, have met their death there.
"May the goddess Śrī, who is both mobile and immobile and possesses a dual form, never abandon those men who, having bathed at Pañcanada, shall worship you. (65)
The illustrious Viṣṇu said: "O Sage Agnibindu, let it be as you have requested here; my name shall exist together with mine by means of half of your name. (66)
O sage, my name shall become renowned throughout the three worlds as Bindumādhava in Kāśī; it shall be the destroyer of the multitude of great sins.
Those meritorious men who shall always worship me here in this meritorious lake of Pañcanada—from where can they have fear of saṃsāra?
Lakṣmī, who is the embodiment of the Vasus and whose name is Nirvāṇa, always dwells by the side of those in whose hearts I reside at Pañcanada.
Those who, having reached the land of the Five Rivers, did not satisfy the twice-born with wealth—for them that wealth weeps, for their misfortunes are swiftly obtained.
They alone are blessed in this world, and they alone have truly accomplished their purpose, by whom my presence has been attained and the Vasus have been made subject to me.
"O Agnibindu, best of sages, this shall be known by your name as Bindutīrtha; it is the destroyer of all sins. (72)
Whoever, devoted to celibacy, bathes at Bindu-tīrtha in the month of Kārtika before the sun has risen—from him, where could there be fear of the daughter of the Sun (Yamunā)? (73)
Even after committing thousands of sins through delusion, a person who bathes in the Dharmanada river during the month of Kārttika becomes sinless in an instant.
As long as this body remains healthy and the senses are not impaired, one should perform religious observances; for religious observance is the fruit of the body.
This body, a vessel for purity, should be thoroughly cleansed by means of eating once a day, eating only at night, likewise eating only what is unasked for, and by fasting. (76)
The Kṛcchra, Cāndrāyaṇa, and other such penances should be performed with great effort, since by observing these vows the impure body attains purity. (77)
When the body has been thoroughly purified by vows, dharma dwells there immovably; wherever the bull (dharma) stands, there wealth and pleasure, along with liberation, abide.
Therefore, those who desire the fruits of the four aims of life should constantly practice the vows, for they bring about the presence of Dharma. (79)
If a person is unable to perform the vows at all times, then, having reached the Cāturmāsya period, he should perform them with great effort.
Sleeping on the ground, celibacy, some restriction regarding food, the rule of eating only once a day and so forth, and constant giving according to one's own capacity. (81)
Furthermore, listening to the Purāṇas and practicing their meaning, as well as keeping an unbroken lamp burning for the great worship of one's chosen deity; 82.
In a place rich with abundant sprouts and seeds, the wise man should diligently avoid coming and going for the sake of the great increase of Dharma.
Those who are established in the four-month vow must not converse with those who are unfit for conversation; they should always maintain silence, or else speak only what is truthful.
One observing the vow should avoid flat beans, lentils, and kodrava grain; one should always remain with those who are pure, and never touch a person who does not observe the vow.
One's teeth, hair, garments, and so forth must always be purified with great effort; furthermore, the practitioner of vows should never entertain undesirable thoughts, even within his own heart.
Whatever fruit may accrue to one observing vows during all twelve months, that same fruit shall be obtained in its entirety by those who maintain the Cāturmāsya vow.
If one lacks the capacity for the vow during even four months, then one who desires the fruit of the year must observe the vow during the month of Kārttika.
For those of dull intellect whose Kārtika month has passed here without the observance of vows, not even a fraction of merit shall remain, for they are of the nature of swine. (89)
When the month of Kārttika has arrived, a meritorious person should perform the Kṛcchra, the Atikṛcchra, or even the Prājāpatya penance according to their capacity.
When the month of Kārttika arrives, the observer of the vow should perform a fast with a single day of interval, or a three-night vow, or a five-night vow, or a seven-night vow. (91)
One should either observe the fortnightly vow (pakṣavrata) or even the monthly fast (māsopoṣaṇa); no one observing a vow should ever render the month of Kārttika fruitless.
When the month of Kārttika has arrived, the observer of the vow should subsist on vegetables, milk, fruits, or even barley as his food. (93)
In the month of Kārttika, a man observing the vow should perform both daily and occasional ablutions; he should practice celibacy during Kārttika, being intent on the fruit of the great vow.
He who, with a pure mind, spends the greater part of the entire year in celibacy, by him celibacy is truly practiced for the whole year.
But he who concludes the month of Kārttika with fasts—by him, even for a single year, a perfect fast has been observed in this world. (96)
The autumn season, which he had spent on a diet of vegetables and milk, was then passed by him on that very same diet without interruption.
In the month of Kārttika, one should eat from leaves; one must avoid bell-metal with great effort. If a person observing the vow eats from bell-metal, he shall not obtain the fruit of that vow.

In the observance of the bell-metal vow, one should give bell-metal filled with clarified butter. In the month of Kārttika, one should not consume honey, for it leads to a very low state of rebirth. (99)
Upon the abandonment of honey, one should offer ghee and milk-rice with sugar; during the month of Ūrja, one should avoid oil for both anointing the body and consumption.
O sinless one, that embodied being who performs oil-massage there shall become a denizen of hell; therefore, upon abandoning the use of oil, one should give a *droṇa* measure of golden sesamum seeds.
He who eats fish in the month of Kārtika enters the womb of a sea-monster; he who eats meat in the month of Bāhula becomes a worm in pus and blood.
Even those kings who are meat-eaters should renounce [meat] during Kārttika; having completely abandoned fish and meat, one should be intent on the vow in Kārttika.

One certainly becomes free from the fault of eating fish and meat by observing the restraint regarding them; on the full moon day of Kārttika, the observer of the vow should give kūṣmāṇḍa gourds along with black gram and ten pieces of gold.
He who eats fish during the month of Kārtika indeed eats nectar itself; being silent, he should cause a fine bell, together with sesame seeds, gold, and a cow, to be given as a gift.
By that virtuous observer of vows who has abandoned salt during the month of Kārtika, all flavors have been renounced; therefore, one who has renounced it should cause a cow to be given as a gift.

One observing the vow who sleeps on the ground during the month of Kārttika should not touch the earth [with his limbs]; one who sleeps on the ground should donate a bed provided with cotton and pillows.
He who offers an unbroken lamp with a ghee-soaked wick during the month of Kārttika does not go to a miserable state of existence, even upon encountering the blinding darkness of delusion.
Whoever should perform the festival of lamps (Dīpakaumudī) during the night in the month of Kārtika shall never behold the darkness of Tāmisra or Andhatāmisra.
One who is enraged by the darkness of sin does not behold the Sun-god, whose face is darkened by anger, as a result of offering lamps during the month of Kārtika.
He shall behold the three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile, as consisting of light; whoever lights a lamp with a bright wick before me, he shall awaken it.
If a person bathes me with jars of the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) during the month of Ūrja, that meritorious one shall reach the shore of the Ocean of Milk and dwell there for a kalpa.
One who, endowed with devotion, offers the moonlight produced by lamps before me every day during the month of Kārttika, shall not enter the darkness of the womb again.
He who kindles a lamp with a ghee-soaked wick before my face shall not suffer a loss of intellect, even when faced with the great terror of death.
For those who, intent on devotion, have performed my pilgrimage in the month of Kārtika and have bathed at Bindu-tīrtha, liberation is not far off.
O Dāmodara, slayer of the lords of the Danujas, accept this arghya from me, who am observing vows and have bathed according to the rules in the month of Kārttika.
O Kṛṣṇa, during this occasional bath in the month of Kārttika which withers away sins, may you, together with Rādhā, accept this arghya offered by me. 17.
The meritorious person, having recited these two mantras, offers me this arghya from a conch shell filled with water, gold, jewels, and flowers.
On that auspicious day, by him the earth filled with gold was duly given to a worthy recipient, preceded by the ritual sprinkling of water and the formal resolve.
Having observed the Ekādaśī that marks my awakening, one who has bathed at Bindutīrtha and remains engaged in a night vigil [attains the fruit]. || 120 ||

Having illuminated many lamps and adorned me according to one's ability, [one should worship] with the diversion of the threefold symphony (tauryatrika), the hearing of Purāṇas, and so forth. || 21 ||
Having performed a great festival until the lunar day is complete, a person should give food in abundance there for my pleasure. (22)
Even one joined with great sins (mahāpātaka) shall not enter the womb of a woman, provided that he worships me here under the name Bindumādhava.
Having bathed at Bindutīrtha, he indeed attains liberation; O Sage, I am named Ādimādhava and am to be worshipped in the Satyayuga.
In the Tretā age, I am to be known as Anantamādhava, the bestower of all perfections; in the Dvāpara age, I am named Śrīdamādhava, the accomplisher of the supreme goal.
In the Kali age, I am to be known as Bindumādhava, the destroyer of the impurities of the Kali age; yet, in the Kali age, men who are filled with sin do not find me.
Deluded by my very own māyā and devoted to the doctrine of duality, those who indeed practice devotion to me yet hate Viśveśvara are truly deluded.
Those enemies of mine should be known as destined for the state of Piśācas; even after having attained a Piśāca womb, they remain so by the command of Kālabhairava. (28)
Having dwelt for thirty thousand years in the ocean of suffering, they shall thereafter attain liberation solely through the grace of Viśveśa.
Therefore, one should not harbor hatred toward the Lord of the Universe, the Supreme Self; for there is no atonement for men who hate the Lord of the Universe.
For those lowest of men who, even in their minds, harbor hatred for the Lord of the Universe in this world, they dwell perpetually in the Andhatāmisra hell after death.
Those who are intent on reviling Śiva and those who revile the Pāśupatas should be known as my enemies; they fall into the impure hell.
Indeed, those who revile the Lord of the Universe shall dwell for an eon after eon in twenty-eight crores of hells, one after another.
Having obtained the grace of Viśveśa, even I am a bestower of liberation; therefore, Viśveśvara should be worshipped incessantly, especially by my devotees.
O Sage, this Vārāṇasī should be known as the sacred site of Paśupati; therefore, Paśupati should be worshipped in Kāśī by those seeking the supreme good. || 35 ||
At this holy site of Pañcanada, Viśveśvara himself always bathes during the month of Kārttika, accompanied by his attendants, Skanda, and all his retinue.
Brahmā with the Vedas, the Sun, the Mothers beginning with Brahmāṇī, the seven oceans along with the rivers—all bathe during the month of Kārttika at Dhūtapāpaka.
For as many conscious embodied beings as there are in the three worlds, so many come to bathe in Kārtika, which washes away all sins.
The lives of those embodied beings who, having reached the auspicious Kārttika month, have not bathed at Pañcanada, are as futile as bubbles upon the water. (39)
The sacred Ānandakānana is meritorious, and Pāñcanada is more meritorious than that; even greater than that, O great sage Agnibindu, is my own presence.
By this very inference, O one of great wisdom, understand the majesty of Pañcanada, which is the most excellent among all sacred fords (tīrthas). || 41 ||
Having heard from the mouth of Viṣṇu that by hearing this even one of great wisdom is liberated from great sins, that great sage Agnibindu [acted accordingly].
Having bowed down once more, he questioned Bindumādhava, the Imperishable One.
Agnibindu said: "O Blessed One, O Bindumādhava, I wish to hear that; please tell me: O Janārdana, how many forms of yours are present in Kāśī?"
O Acyuta, tell me which of those that are yet to come shall be honored here, by worshipping which my devotees will attain the fulfillment of their purpose. (145)

Thus ends the sixtieth chapter, titled "The Manifestation of Bindumādhava," in the latter half of the Kāśī-khaṇḍa, within the fourth section of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 60 ||
Agastya said: O Six-faced One, I have heard the account of Mādhava which destroys all sins, and I have also properly heard the supreme majesty of Pañcanada.
Relate the answer that was given by Madhusūdana to Agnibindu when he questioned Mādhava, exactly as it was told by the enemy of Madhu.
Skanda said: Listen, O great sage Agastya, to that which is being told by me now, just as it was related by Mādhava to the sage Agnibindu.
Bindumādhava said: "O Agnibindu of great wisdom, know me first as Ādikeśava in the Pādodaka Tīrtha, the bestower of liberation upon devotees. (4)
Those who worship Ādikeśava in the immortal field of Avimukta certainly attain immortality, being freed from all suffering.
Having installed the great Liṅga Saṃgameśa, Ādikeśava shall always bestow both worldly enjoyment and liberation upon men through its mere sight, which destroys their sins.
To the south of Pādodaka is the most excellent Śvetadvīpa-tīrtha; there, known as Jñānakeśava, I bestow knowledge upon men.
Having bathed in Śvetadvīpa in the presence of Jñānakeśava, a person never falls away from knowledge by virtue of worshipping Jñānakeśava.
I am named Tārkṣyakeśava; at Tārkṣyatīrtha, I am always to be worshipped with devotion by the best of men. O Tārkṣya, you are as dear to me as he.
In that very place, at the Nārada-tīrtha, I am known as Nāradakeśava; I am the instructor of the knowledge of Brahman for those whose bodies have been bathed in that sacred ford.
Right there is the Prahlāda-tīrtha, where I am known by the name Prahlādakeśava; I am to be worshipped by devotees for the sake of attaining abundant great devotion.
At that holy ford, Ambarīṣa, I am known by the name Ādityakeśava; there, I destroy the mass of darkness that is sin even by a mere glance.
To the south of Dattātreyeśvara, I am Gadādhara, the primordial one; there I remove the entire accumulation of the disease of saṃsāra for my devotees.
In that very Bhārgava Tīrtha, at the place known as Bhṛgukeśava, I sustain with my heart's desires those men who dwell in Kāśī.
In the great and auspicious holy site named Vāmana, which grants the heart's desires, I am to be worshipped by those seeking welfare under the name Vāmanakeśava.
At the Nara-Nārāyaṇa Tīrtha, by worshipping me—who am of the nature of Nara and Nārāyaṇa—the devotees shall indeed become of the nature of Nara and Nārāyaṇa. (16)
At the sacred ford known as Yajñavarāha, I am to be worshipped by men who desire the fruits of all sacrifices under the name Yajñavārāha. (17)
I am Vidāranarasiṃha, the destroyer of obstacles in Kāśī; I should be worshipped at the holy site bearing my name for the pacification of disturbances to the sacred place.
Having worshipped me with devotion at the Gopīgoviṃda Tīrtha under the name Gopīgoviṃda, a person shall not be touched by my Māyā.
O Sage, I am Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha; in this purifying sacred ford named after me, I bestow the most auspicious prosperity through constant gifts upon those endowed with devotion.
I, named Śeṣamādhava, bestow all special boons desired by my devotees at the sin-destroying Śeṣatīrtha. (21)
Having bathed at the Śaṅkhamādhava Tīrtha and having bathed me, Śaṅkhamādhava, with water from a conch, one shall become the lord of the treasure of the conch (Śaṅkhanidhi).
Having bowed down to me, Hayagrīvakeśava, at the great holy site of Hayagrīva, one shall surely attain that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
I am named Bhīṣmakeśava, located to the west of Vṛddhakāleśa; when served with devotion, I remove terrible obstacles.
I am Nirvāṇakeśava, the indicator of liberation for my devotees; O Hara, the fickleness of the mind [is removed] on the northern side of Lolārka.
He who worships me in Kāśī as Tribhuvanakeśava, renowned in the three worlds and worthy of worship by the most beautiful woman in the three realms, shall not enter a womb again.
Know me as Jñānamādhava in the front part of the Jñānavāpī; by worshipping me there with devotion, one attains eternal knowledge.
Known by the name Śvetamādhava, I shall, having been duly worshipped with devotion, assume the form of the Lord of Śvetadvīpa in the presence of Viśālākṣī.
Having bathed well at the sacred site of Prayāga and beheld me, Mādhava, who am known as Prayāga and who possess ten successful horse-sacrifices, one is liberated from all sins. (29)
Whatever fruit is heard in the scriptures for men who go to Prayāga through austerity, that same fruit shall be tenfold by bathing here in my presence.
Whatever merit belongs to those who bathe at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, ten times that merit shall be obtained here in Kāśī in my presence.
Whatever fruit may accrue to those giving gifts when the sun is eclipsed by Rāhu, that same fruit—indeed ten times greater—shall be obtained right here at Kāśī in Kurukṣetra. || 32 ||
Where the Gaṅgā flows northward and the Yamunā flows eastward, a man who reaches their confluence is liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin.
There, shaving of the head should be performed and the offering of funeral cakes (piṇḍas) should be made with devotion; gifts should be given there by one desiring great fruit.
All those qualities which have been proclaimed as existing in the field of Prajāpati indeed become innumerable in the great field of Avimukta. || 35 ||
The great Liṅga Prayāgeśa, which grants all desires, resides there; and because of its presence, that holy site is celebrated as the granter of all desires.
For those who have not bathed at Prayāga during the month of Māgha when the sun is in Capricorn at Kāśī, having reached the dawn [of the new year], whence can there be ultimate liberation? (37)
Those who, being self-controlled, bathe during the month of Kārttika at Prayāga while engaged in austerity, will certainly obtain the fruit produced by ten horse-sacrifices.
Those who, having bathed at Prayāga during the month of Māgha, always worship daily with devotion Prayāgamādhava and Prayāgeśa, the granter of desires; || 39 ||
Having obtained wealth, grain, sons, and prosperity, and having enjoyed delightful pleasures here on earth, they shall attain supreme bliss and ultimate liberation.
Indeed, during the month of Māgha, all sacred fords from the east, north, west, south, as well as from below and above, come together at Prayāga.
O Sage, the holy places situated in Kāśī do not go anywhere; if they were to go, they would go only to the three unsurpassed holy places.
Every morning at dawn, they come into my presence at Pañcanada during the month of Kārttika—a place that pacifies the flood of great sins and bestows supreme welfare.
Having reached Māgha, the enemy of Agha (Kāma), in the vicinity of Prayāgeśa, all the holy fords bathe at Prayāga in the morning along with me.
Having reached midday, they always proceed toward Maṇikarṇikā, the bestower of liberation, in order to bathe in all the sacred fords (tīrthas).
O Sage, this supreme secret regarding Kāśī has been told to you, concerning how the triad of sacred fords is most excellent at their respective times in particular. || 46 ||
I shall speak another secret that must not be disclosed anywhere; it is always to be concealed from those who lack devotion, but it is not to be concealed from one who possesses devotion.
In Kāśī, all sacred fords (tīrthas), each one surpassing the next, forcibly destroy even great sins by their own inherent splendor. (48)
This very secret concerning Vārāṇasī is proclaimed to you: raising up a single finger, it is the truth that Maṇikarṇikā alone is the most excellent. 49.
Alas! All the holy fords (tīrthas), each remaining in its own station, roar out only after attaining the exceedingly great power of Māṇikarṇika.
Having destroyed even great and numerous sins of sinners at midday, he went to the holy sites of Kāśī with the desire to perform expiation.
Whether on the auspicious festival days or even on ordinary days, those who always observe their vows certainly become stainless after plunging into Maṇikarṇikā.
The Lord of the Universe, together with Viśvā, having reached Maṇikarṇika every day at midday, performs his ritual bath daily.
O sage, even from Vaikuṇṭha, I always plunge into Maṇikarṇikā at midday together with Padmā, with supreme joy.
Since I remove the sins of those who utter my name even once, by the power of that name which has entered [my being], I am Māṇikarṇika.
Every day, the Grandfather Brahmā, traveling on his swan-vehicle from Satyaloka, arrives at Maṇikarṇikā for the performance of his midday rites.
Indra and the other guardians of the world, as well as Marīci and the other great sages, gathered at Maṇikarṇikā to perform their midday rites.
And Śeṣa, Vāsuki, and the other chief nāgas indeed come here from the world of the nāgas at midday to bathe in Maṇikarṇikā.
As many sentient beings as there are among all things moving and stationary, so many bathe at midday in the pure waters of Maṇikarṇikā.
O Brahmin, who is capable of describing the exceedingly great qualities of the Māṇikarṇikeya [deities], which are beyond numbering and [unassailable] by pride and other such passions? (60)
Fierce austerities were performed by those whose wealth is penance in the forests, by whom this Maṇikarṇikā—the ground of liberation—has indeed been attained.
Only those bulls among men have truly bestowed great gifts who, in their final years, have reached this Maṇikarṇikā.
Those by whom the soft ground of Māṇikarṇikā has been made their own bed have certainly fulfilled all their vows according to the prescribed injunctions. (63)
They alone are truly blessed among mortals who, having renounced the prosperity acquired through merit, have beheld Maṇikarṇikā after being initiated into all the sacrifices.
Those men who, having reached old age, attained Maṇikarṇikā, had performed various kinds of religious duties, including sacrifices and works of public utility.
Jewels, fine silken garments, gold, elephants, and horses—these should always be diligently offered by a wise person along with the Maṇikarṇikā.
O Sage, even a very small amount of wealth acquired through merit, when given by those men, becomes eternal and inexhaustible, like the water in Maṇikaṇikā.
Even a single breath-control (prāṇāyāma) performed as prescribed by that best of men surely constitutes the supreme six-limbed yoga (ṣaḍaṅga-yoga).
Having reached Maṇikarṇikā and recited even a single Gāyatrī mantra, one clearly obtains the fruit of reciting the Gāyatrī ten thousand times. || 69 ||
By offering even a single oblation near Maṇikarṇikā, a wise person obtains the complete fruit of performing the Agnihotra sacrifice for as long as he lives.
Having heard these words of Hari, Agnibindu, of great asceticism, prostrated with great devotion and questioned Mādhava once again.
Agnibindu said: O Viṣṇu, O lotus-eyed one, how great is the extent of this meritorious Maṇikarṇikā? Tell me, for there is no one other than you who knows the truth.
Śrī Viṣṇu said: Maṇikarṇikā extends from Gaṅgā Keśava to the pavilion of Hariścandra, from the middle of the celestial river (Devasarit) to Svardvāra.
I shall describe to you this gross measurement as well as the subtle one: at the front of the Hariścandra Tīrtha is Hariścandravināyaka.
And here, to the north of the Maṇikarṇī pool, is Sīmāvināyaka; having worshipped Sīmāvināyaka with devotion, the best of men [attains his goal]. (75)
One should reach Maṇikarṇikā with offerings of sweetmeats and ritual services; at the great holy site of Hariścandra, one should offer libations to the ancestors.
A man who, endowed with faith, bathes in the great holy site of Hariścandra, shall remain satisfied for a hundred years and shall grant whatever is desired.
Having bowed to Hariścandreśvara, one does not fall away from truth; thereafter is Parvatatīrtha, in the vicinity of Parvateśvara.
The sacred site of Mahāmeru destroys even the greatest of sins; having bathed there, worshipped the Lord, and given something according to one's ability, [one attains the fruit]. (79)
Having occupied the peak of Mount Meru, one enjoys divine pleasures. To the south of Parvateśvara is the Kambalāśvatara Tīrtha. (80)
And to the west of that holy site is the auspicious Kaṃbalāśvatareśa; he who bathes in that holy site and worships that Liṅga [shall attain merit]. || 81 ||
Moreover, those born in his family shall be skilled in song and endowed with prosperity; there, the Cakrapuṣkariṇī is the remover of the cycle of rebirth.
In this dense wheel of saṃsāra, where one who has bathed may not enter again, there is the Cakrapuṣkariṇī tīrtha, my supreme abode. 83.
For as many years as there are in the number of a parārdha, he performed great penance there; there, the Supreme Lord of the Universe became manifest before my very eyes.
There, I obtained sovereignty that is imperishable and most extensive; and the Cakrapuṣkariṇī became renowned as Maṇikarṇikā. (85)
Having abandoned her liquid form and assumed the form of a woman, Maṇikarṇikā was seen by me there in manifest, embodied form. 86.
I shall describe her form, which bestows supreme auspiciousness upon devotees; by meditating on that form for six months at the three junctions of the day, [men attain their goal]. || 87 ||
The goddess Maṇikarṇikā is seen in her manifest form, four-armed, large-eyed, with a radiant eye upon her forehead. 88.
She is always facing westward with her hands joined in a perpetual gesture of prayer, holding a garland of blue lotuses in her right hand.
In her auspicious right hand she holds a *mātuluṅga* fruit; she eternally possesses the form of a young maiden and is perpetually twelve years of age.
She possessed the luster of pure crystal and had beautiful, dark-blue, glossy hair; her lovely lips surpassed coral and rubies in beauty.

Her head was adorned with a beautiful braided hair-tuft featuring fresh ketakī flowers; her entire body was decorated with pearl ornaments, and she was draped in a garment with the luster of the moon.
Bearing a beautiful garland made of lotuses upon her heart, she should be meditated upon in this form day and night by those seeking liberation.

The glorious Maṇikarṇikā is the abode of the splendor of Nirvāṇa; I shall now declare its mantra, known as the "Wish-fulfilling Tree for Devotees," by the recitation of which even the eight supernatural powers (siddhis) are attained by men. (94)

First, one should utter the Vāgbhava, Māyā, Lakṣmī, Madana, and Praṇava; then the word "Bhānti" ending with a Bindu, followed by the word "Maṇi"; then, on the pericarp (karṇikā), [the mantra] enclosed by the Heart and the Praṇava.

This mantra, equal to the celestial wish-fulfilling tree, bestows a continuous succession of all happiness when recited; its syllables are measured by the lunar days (tithis), and it grants the supreme state to those of sharp intellect. 96.

The syllable *tāra* (om), followed by the third *tāra* (om) ending with a bindu, then the word *maṇi*, then the word *karṇike*, then the word *praṇavātmi*, and finally the word *kena ma*; this mantra consists of sixteen syllables.

This mantra should be recited incessantly by men desiring liberation; a fire-offering (homa) consisting of one-tenth the number of recitations should be performed by those men who are bound by faith and full of devotion.
The wise man, always pure, [should offer] blooming white lotuses, cow’s ghee, sugar, and honey.
By reciting this mantra three hundred thousand times, even if one dies in another land, one will certainly attain liberation through the power of this mantra. (100)
An image made of gold, endowed with the nine gems and possessing the form previously described, should be fashioned; it must be worshipped with great care.
Having worshipped it constantly in the home, men who desire only liberation should then carefully worship it and cast it into Maṇikarṇikā.
Those men who fear cyclic existence and possess devotion bound by faith should practice this means here, even if they dwell far away. (3)
Having bathed at Maṇikarṇikā and beheld the Lord Maṇikarṇīśa, a person shall not dwell again within the womb of a mother.
The Maṇikarṇīśvara Liṅga was formerly installed by me; it should be worshipped here at the eastern door of the inner sanctum by those desiring liberation.
Then, to the south of Maṇikarṇika, there is the Pāśupata Tīrtha; having performed the water-rites there, one should behold Paśupatīśvara.
Therein the Pāśupata Yoga was taught by the wielder of the Pināka bow; it is that which removes the bonds of the individual soul (paśu) even for me and for the gods headed by Brahmā.
Therefore, Paśupati himself, assuming the form of a liṅga, eternally manifests in Kāśī for the sake of liberating bound souls from their fetters.
There, on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, a pilgrimage should be performed with effort by those of pure mind, as well as a vigil at night.
Having worshipped Paśupati and being devoted to fasting, those who break their fast on the new moon day are not bound by the fetters of the individual soul (paśu-pāśa).
Beyond that is the holy site of Rudrāvāsa, situated before the Pāśupata tīrtha; having bathed there, men should worship Hara as Rudrāvāseśvara.
By worshipping Rudrāvāseśvara to the south of Maṇikarṇīśvara, a person shall dwell in the world of Rudrāvāsa; of this there is no doubt.
Then, to the south, is Viśvatīrtha, presided over by all the sacred fords (tīrthas). Having bathed there with devotion, a person should behold Viśvanātha.
Thereafter, having worshipped Viśvā and Gaurī with supreme devotion, one becomes worthy of worship by the universe and subsequently becomes identical with the universe. || 14 ||
Thereafter, having performed his ablutions at Muktitīrtha, and then having worshipped Mokṣeśvara, he undoubtedly attains liberation.
After beholding Mokṣeśa to the west of Avimukteśvara, a person, alas, does not undergo the coming and going again in the world of mortals.
The holy site of Avimukteśvara is slightly superior even to the holy sites of liberation; having bathed there and worshipped Avimukteśa, one is liberated.
Beyond that is the Tāraka Tīrtha, where Viśveśvara himself imparts the Tāraka Brahman—the essence of nectar—into the ear of one whose ears have become immortal.
Having bathed well at the Tāraka-tīrtha and beheld Tārakeśvara, one crosses the ocean of worldly existence and delivers even one's ancestors.
In its vicinity is Skanda-tīrtha; having bathed there and beheld the Six-faced One (Kārttikeya), that best of men shall cast off his body composed of the six qualities.
Having seen the six-faced god to the east of Tārakeśvara, one shall dwell in the world of Ṣaḍānana, bearing a youthful form.
Then, at the meritorious Ḍhuṇḍhitīrtha, a man who has performed his water-libations and has praised Gaṇapati Ḍhuṇḍhi is not overcome by obstacles.
There is the incomparable Bhavānī-tīrtha to the south of Ḍhuṇḍhi-tīrtha; having bathed there according to the prescribed rite and having fully worshipped Bhavānī, [one attains the fruit]. || 23 ||
Having worshipped Bhavānī with fine silken garments, jeweled ornaments, extensive food offerings, flowers, incense, and lamps; || 54 ||
By those who have worshipped Bhavānī and Śaṅkara in Kāśī with faith, the entire three worlds, including all things mobile and immobile, have been worshipped.
On the eighth day of the month of Caitra, the wise man should perform the great procession of Bhavānī; one hundred and eight circumambulations should be performed.
By him the earth, consisting of seven islands, along with its mountains, oceans, hermitages, and forests, has been circumambulated clockwise.
Those intent on his satisfaction should offer eight circumambulations every day; Bhavānī and Śaṅkara should always be bowed to with great effort. (28)
Bhavānī is the eternal bestower of desires upon her devotees and the giver of garments; therefore, Bhavānī should be worshipped in Kāśī by those residing at the holy sites.
Bhavānī shall always provide for the welfare and security of those who dwell in Kāśī; therefore, Bhavānī should be constantly worshipped by the residents of Kāśī.
Alms should always be sought by a monk who desires liberation, because in Kāśī, the wife of Viśveśvara is the giver of alms. (31)
In the middle of this house is Viśveśa, with Bhavānī as his consort; he bestows the alms of liberation upon all who reside in Kāśī. || 32 ||
Whatever may be difficult to attain for those dwelling in the sacred field of Kāśī, Bhavānī, when worshipped by men, makes that very thing easily obtainable. (33)
On the Mahāṣṭamī, the man observing the vow should keep a vigil at night; by worshipping Bhavānī in the morning, he shall obtain his desired fruit.
He who beholds Bhavānī in the western direction from Śukreśa—his every desire shall be fulfilled in this world; of this there is no doubt. || 35 ||
One should always reside in Kāśī and bathe in the north-flowing river; Bhavānī and Śaṅkara should be served, for both worldly enjoyment and liberation are to be attained there.

O Mother Bhavānī, may I become the dust of your feet; O Mother Bhavānī, may I become even more of your servant. O Mother Bhavānī, may I not be "non-existent" (na-bhavāni) as long as I exist in this world, but rather may I be one who shares in your nature (tvad-bhāg-bhavāni) every day, and never again be subject to rebirth (punar-bhavāni). 37.
Whether standing or walking, sleeping or waking, this [mantra] should always be recited here by a resident of Kāśī for the attainment of happiness. (38)
Right there, in the vicinity of the Bhavānī-tīrtha, is the Īśāna-tīrtha; he who bathes there and worships Īśāna shall not be subject to rebirth.
And right there is Jñānatīrtha, which always bestows knowledge upon men; having performed one's ablutions in that holy ford and beheld Śiva as Jñāneśvara, [one attains liberation]. (140)
For those by whom Jñāneśa, situated near Jñānavāpī, has been duly worshipped, there shall be no loss of knowledge even when they meet their death.

Right there is the Śailādi-tīrtha, which manifests supreme prosperity; having performed the śrāddha and other rites there, and having given gifts according to one's ability, [one attains great merit]. (42)
Having beheld Śailādīśvara in the northern direction of Jñānavāpī, one shall attain the status of a Gaṇa; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
To the south of Naṃditīrtha is my supreme Viṣṇutīrtha; by offering funeral cakes (piṇḍas) there, one becomes free from debt to the ancestors.
He who, having performed his ablutions at Viṣṇutīrtha, beholds me as Viṣṇu on the southern side of Viśveśa, goes to the world of Viṣṇu.
He who, having reached Pratyekādaśī, as well as Śayanī and Bodhinī, performs a vigil at night in the vicinity of my image; || 46 ||
Having worshipped me with devotion in the morning and having fed the twice-born, and having given cows, gold, and land, one shall not be born again as a partaker of the earth.
Having performed the formal conclusion of the vow there, free from stinginess regarding wealth, the wise person shall indeed obtain the full fruit of the vow by my command. (48)
To the south of my sacred ford (tīrtha) is the auspicious Paitāmaha tīrtha; having gratified the ancestors there by means of the performance of the śrāddha rite, [one attains the highest goal].
Having worshipped with devotion the Pitāmaheśvara Liṅga situated above the Brahma-nāla, a person shall attain the world of Brahmā. || 150 ||

Any action, whether auspicious or inauspicious, performed in the vicinity of the stream of Brahmā (Brahmasrotas) attains supreme imperishability; therefore, one should perform only that which is auspicious.
O best of sages, whatever action—whether auspicious or inauspicious—is performed here, even if it be very slight, there is no dissolution of that [karma] even at the time of universal dissolution.
This is declared to be the Nābhi-tīrtha because it is the navel of the earth; indeed, this auspicious source is the very navel of the cosmic egg.
This is the navel of Māṇikarṇikā, the ground of profundity, wherein the entire cosmic egg undergoes both dissolution and emergence. (54)
The Brahmānala is a supreme holy ford, renowned throughout the three worlds; having bathed at its confluence, a person may remove the impurities of ten million births.
Even those whose mere bones might fall within the stalk of Brahmā never enter the interior of the pavilion of the cosmic egg.
Then, to the south of the Bhāgīrathī-tīrtha and the Brahmanāla, a man who bathes there properly is liberated from the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa.
The Bhāgīrathīśvara Liṅga is located in the vicinity of Svargadvāra; by its sight, the expiation for the sin of killing a Brahmin is said to be accomplished.
He whose ancestors have fallen into an inauspicious state of existence must diligently offer libations at the Bhāgīrathī Tīrtha.
Having performed the Śrāddha rite according to the rules at that Bhāgīrathī Tīrtha and having fed the Brāhmaṇas, one leads one's ancestors to the world of Brahmā.
To the south of that is the great sacred site known as Khurakartari, so called because of the tips of the hooves of the cows who came from Goloka.
Then, at that sacred ford where the ground was made uneven by the marks of his hooves, he performed his ablutions and completed the rites of offering water and funeral cakes.
Upon seeing the Khurakartarīśa Liṅga, one shall attain Goloka; by worshipping that Liṅga, one shall never be deprived of wealth in cattle.
To the south, by Khurakartarī, is the supreme Mārkaṇḍa Tīrtha; having performed the rite of Śrāddha in that sin-destroying Tīrtha, [one attains the highest goal]. 64.
By beholding the Mārkaṇḍeyeśvara Liṅga, one shall obtain long life, an increase in Brahmanic luster, and supreme fame upon the earth.
The Vasiṣṭha-tīrtha is supreme and destroys even the greatest sins; having offered libations to the ancestors there and beheld Vasiṣṭheśa, [one attains purification].
A person is not tainted by sins accumulated over three lifetimes; endowed with Brahmanic luster, he dwells in the world of Vasiṣṭha.
Right there is the Aruḍhaṃtī Tīrtha, which destroys the good fortune of women; that Tīrtha should especially be bathed in by women devoted to their husbands.
The fault born of unchastity shall, by bathing at that sacred ford, meet its destruction in an instant through the power of Arundhatī. (69)
By worshipping Vasiṣṭheśvara to the east of Mārkaṇḍeyeśvara, a mortal becomes free from sin and attains great merit.
If the images of Vasiṣṭha and Arundhatī are worshipped there with great effort, a woman does not suffer widowhood, nor does a man suffer separation from his wife.
To the south of Vasiṣṭhatīrtha is the excellent Narmadātīrtha; having performed the śrāddha there and beheld the Lord of the Narmadā, the wise man [attains his goal].

Having given a great gift there, one is liberated by means of the Padma vehicle; thereafter, at the holy ford Trisandhya, located to the east of Trisandhyeśvara, [one should worship] during the three junctions of the day.

Having bathed at that sacred ford and performed the twilight devotions (saṃdhyā) according to the prescribed rule, a person is not overcome by the sins arising from the omission of the twilight prayers.

Having beheld Trisaṃdhyeśvara and performed the twilight rites at the three times of day, a twice-born man who acts with faith shall obtain the merit arising from reciting the three Vedas three times over.
Then, having performed an ablution there at the Anuyoginī Tīrtha and beholding the Yoginī-pīṭha, a man shall attain perfection in yoga. || 76 ||
There exists the Agasti Tīrtha, which destroys a great multitude of sins; having bathed there with diligence and beheld the omnipresent Lord Agastīśvara, [one attains liberation].
Then, having offered libations to the ancestors at Agastikuṇḍa, and having bowed down to Lopāmudrā together with Agasti; || 78 ||
Freed from all sins and divested of all afflictions, that best of men shall go to the world of Śiva together with his ancestors.
To the south of Agastya-tīrtha, there is a most purifying holy site known as Gaṅgākeśava, which destroys all sins.
There, O Sage, the wise man who worships with faith my auspicious form known by the name of that sacred ford (tīrtha) is glorified in my world.
Having offered funeral cakes there and given gifts according to his ability, he shall present to the ancestors a satisfaction lasting for a hundred years.
This great extent of Maṇikarṇikā has been proclaimed to you; it extends as far as the Sīmāvināyaka to the south, because it destroys all obstacles.
To the east of Vairocanīśvara, I am Vaikuṇṭha-Mādhava; by worshipping me there with devotion, one shall attain the state of Vaikuṇṭha.
O Sage, I am known as Vīramādhava, located to the west of Vīreśa; having worshipped me there while observing a vow, one shall not suffer the torments of Yama.
I am named Kālamādhava; in the presence of Kālabhairava, it is certain that neither the Kali age nor Time shall affect my devotee. (86)
Having fasted on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa and having performed a vigil there, one shall never behold Yama.
I am Nirvāṇanarasiṃha, located to the south of Pulastīśvara; even by bowing to my form, a devotee attains liberation.
O Sage, this Greatly Powerful Man-Lion (Mahābala-Nṛsiṃha) is situated to the east of the syllable Oṃ; the worshipper of that [deity] shall not see the messengers of Yama, who possess great strength.
I am Pracaṇḍanarasiṃha, situated to the east of Caṇḍabhairava; even by committing a most violent sin, one becomes free from all evil through the worship of Him.
I am Girinṛsiṃha, who, from the Vināyaka of that very body, stands in the east as the tearer asunder of the elephants of the mass of powerful sins.
O great sage, I am Narasiṃha, the remover of great fear; after Pitāmaha and Īśvara, I am the one who trembles before the trembling of my devotees.
I am the most formidable Narasiṃha, located to the west of Kalaśeśvara; when worshipped with faith, I destroy even the most terrible flood of sins.
I am Jvālāmālīnṛsiṃha; being fully worshipped in the presence of Jvālāmukhī, I consume the heaps of sins like blades of grass with my blazing flame.
I am Kolāhalanṛsiṃha, the crusher of Daityas and Dānavas; for by the utterance of my name, the tumultuous clamor of sin is brought to an end.
Where Kaṅkālabhairava, whose intellect is expert in protecting Kāśī, resides—having worshipped me there with devotion, one is not obstructed by calamities. (96)
I am Viṭaṅkanarasiṃha, located after Nīlakaṇṭheśvara; by worshipping me there with faith, a person becomes free from fear.
I am Ananta-Vamana; in the presence of the Lord, even the infinite impurities of a devotee are removed when Hari is worshipped. (98)
I am known by the name Dadhivāmana; I bestow curd-rice upon my devotees, by the mere remembrance of whose name a man shall never become poor. (99)
I am Trivikrama in Kāśī, located to the north of Trilocana; when worshipped, I bestow prosperity and I also remove all sins.
I am named Bali-vāmana; I am fully worshipped by Bali. To the east of Balibhadreśvara, I increase the strength of my devotees. || 11 ||
"I have come here from Tāmradvīpa, located to the south of Bhavattīrtha; I am known by the name Tāmravarāha, the bestower of desired objects upon my devotees. (2)
O Sage, the Boar-incarnation of the Earth, having bathed here at Vārāhatīrtha in the presence of Prayāgeśvara and beheld me in the form of a boar, [proceeded]. || 3 ||
Having worshipped with great devotion, one shall not enter the confinement of the womb; by giving even a small amount of food there, one obtains the fruit of the gift of the earth.
A person falling into the deep ocean of great impurity does not sink even at the time of universal dissolution, provided they have obtained the raft of devotion to me.
I am Kokāvarāha, located near Kiṭīśvara; by worshipping me there, a mortal obtains his desired fruit.
There were one hundred and five Nārāyaṇas, fifty who recline upon the waters, thirty in the form of tortoises, and twenty in the form of fish.
There are one hundred and eight Gopālas, and Buddhas exist by the thousands; there are thirty Rāmas, and one hundred and one Rāmas.
"I alone am the form of Viṣṇu in the midst of the pavilion of liberation; by the grace of the sage, I have been personally resorted to by the Lord of the Universe."
In the form of Nārāyaṇa, six hundred thousand Gaṇas, with discuses and maces raised, provide protection for the sacred field on all sides.
Having heard [the name] "Sognibiṃdu," his hair stood on end with joy; the wise one asked again: "O Lord, tell me once more of the different forms [of the deity]. (11)
For the welfare of Your own devotees and for the pacification of my doubt, O Infinite One, tell me: how many are Your forms, and how are they to be known? (12)
Having heard these words of Agnibindu, the treasury of asceticism, the Blessed Viṣṇu spoke of the successive manifestations of his forms.
Indeed, even by hearing them, a mortal shall not fall into the domain of Yama; thus did Prajāpati proclaim the twenty-four divisions beginning with Keśava.
Śrī Viṣṇu said: O Agnibindu, O highly wise one, listen; I shall tell it to you. Know, O sage, that [the lineage] proceeds from the first right hand according to the order of creation.
Know this form to be that of Keśava, characterized by the conch, discus, mace, and lotus; when worshipped, it unfailingly fulfills the desired objects of men. (16)
The Slayer of Madhu (Viṣṇu) is to be fully known through the conch, the lotus, the mace, and the sword; by serving His form, enemies meet their destruction. (17)
Saṃkarṣaṇa, armed with the conch, lotus, discus, and mace, is to be worshipped here; by worshipping his form, a living being shall never again be subject to rebirth.
Dāmodara is worshipped with the conch, the Kaumodakī mace, the discus, and the lotus; he indeed bestows wealth, sons, cattle, and grain. (19)
Vāmana, characterized by the conch, discus, lotus, and mace, brings prosperity to a person even when worn within the home.
Pradyumna—who possesses the Pāñcajanya conch, the mace, the lotus, the variegated form, and the Sudarśana disc—is worshipped by mortals; he bestows great splendor.
The group of six beginning with Viṣṇu is said to be [emanated] from the upper left hand by the process of emanation (sṛṣṭi); by the mere remembrance of which heaps of sins are dissolved.

For the sake of prosperity, Viṣṇu should be worshipped by men with the conch, discus, mace, and lotus; Mādhava, the bestower of supreme prosperity, [is worshipped] with the conch, lotus, mace, and discus.
Aniruddha, holding aloft the conch, lotus, discus, and mace, should be meditated upon for the sake of perfect accomplishment; likewise Puruṣottama, with the conch, mace, discus, and lotus.

O Sage, Janārdana—the one beyond the senses, the remover of birth, who holds the conch, the discus, the lotus, and the mace—should be meditated upon with the conch, the Kaumodakī mace, the lotus, and the discus. 25.
From the downward-left hand, by way of emanation, are the six forms beginning with Govinda; Govinda always bears the conch, the discus, the mace, and the lotus.

Trivikrama, worshipped with a conch, lotus, mace, and discus, is for the sake of prosperity (lakṣmī); Śrīdhara, bearing a conch, lotus, and discus, and holding a mace, is for the sake of fortune (śrī).
Hṛṣīkeśa is considered to be represented by the conch, mace, discus, and lotus; Nṛsiṃha is understood by means of the conch, discus, lotus, and mace.
Acyuta always holds the conch, mace, lotus, and discus; from the lower right hand onwards, the six [forms] beginning with Vāsudeva are to be understood.
Vāsudeva always bears the conch, the discus, the mace, and the lotus; Nārāyaṇa, likewise bearing the conch, the lotus, the mace, and the discus, is to be meditated upon by men. (230)
O Sage, Upendra should be known as possessing a conch, a lotus, a lotus-navel, a discus, and a mace; he is eternally endowed with a conch, a mace, a discus, and the lotus as his weapon.
Hari, the bearer of the conch, the discus, the lotus, and the mace, removes the sins of men; Kṛṣṇa is so called because of his conch, his mace, his lotus, and his discus. (32)
O great sage, these manifestations of my own forms have been declared by me; by knowing them, a mortal certainly attains both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
While Govinda was speaking thus to the sage Agnibindu, the lord of birds, having fanned away his adversaries with his wings, came into the range of vision.
Having prostrated, Hṛṣīkeśa joyfully announced the arrival of the Three-eyed One; then, with agitation, he asked, "Where is the Lord? (35).
Garuḍa said: Let this one whose banner bears the great bull be made manifest, whose jeweled radiance from the standard shall fill these two worlds, heaven and earth.
Capable of making the construction of the Lokāloka mountain successful, it illuminates the faces of the quarters with the brilliance of ten million suns.
The lotus-eyed one beheld the bull-bannered Lord of the Three Eyes, while the courtyard of the sky was filled with the multitudes of celestial chariots belonging to those traveling in vimānas.
The mountain caves resounded with the floods of sound from great musical instruments, and it was made fragrant by handfuls of flowers scattered by Vidyādharīs.
Having bowed from afar with his hair standing on end in joy, the wielder of the conch, discus, and mace resolved to rise up.
Then Agnibindu, the ocean of joy and bestower of liberation, spoke: "Touch this Sudarśana disc with your right hand."
He was called Agnibindu; as soon as he touched the Sudarśana [discus], he became Sudarśana himself through the supreme grace of Hari.
Skanda said: O Pot-born one, that sage, whose form was light, then became one with Kaustubha, the embodiment of lights, through his service to Bindumādhava.
O Agastya, those whose minds have become bees at the lotus feet of Bindumādhava certainly attain a state comparable to that of Agnibindu.
One must always reside in Kāśī, behold Bindumādhava, listen to this narrative, and conquer the goal of the worlds. (45)
The origin of the Five Rivers is meritorious, the discourse concerning Mādhava is meritorious, and residence in Vārāṇasī is meritorious; these may come to pass for those of meritorious birth.
Whoever shall recite this hymn of praise to Agnibindu here in the presence of Mādhava, having all his desires fulfilled, shall become a lord of the fortune of liberation.
At the time of a śrāddha ceremony, this supreme narrative should always be recited before the twice-born as they eat, for the sake of their ultimate satisfaction. 48.
This narrative should be recited with great devotion during the festival days, in the holy vicinity of Pañcanada, for the increase of meritorious fortune. (49)
This account of the origin of Bindumādhava should be recited with effort and heard with supreme devotion for the sake of attaining both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (250)
When the day of Viṣṇu has arrived, one who observes a vigil at night and hears this meritorious narrative shall obtain residence in Vaikuṇṭha. || 251 ||

Thus ends the sixty-first chapter, titled "The Manifestation of Bindumādhava, the Dialogue between Mādhava and Agnibindu, and the Description of the Greatness of the Vaiṣṇava Tīrtha," in the latter half of the Kāśī-khaṇḍa, the fourth section of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Agastya said: O Skanda, having heard this narrative concerning Bindumādhava, which you have related from your own mouth, I am not yet satiated; it is truly most wonderful.
Now I wish to hear about the assembly of the God of gods; having heard from Tārkṣya of the conduct of Divodāsa, the Three-eyed Lord [desires to hear it].
And what did he say regarding the manifestation of Viṣṇu’s Māyā and the one whose banner bears Garuḍa? And who were those who came together with Śambhu from Mount Mandara? (3)
How was the Lord of Brahmā seen by him whose eyes were agitated with shame? O God, what did he say to Brahmā, and what was said by the Radiant One as well?
"What was said by the Yoginīs? What did those who were ashamed before the Gaṇas say? Tell me this, O Skanda, for I have a great curiosity."
Having heard this question from the sage born from a water-jar (Agastya), Īśa, having offered salutations to Śiva and Pārvatī—the bestowers of success upon those who bow before them—replied.
Skanda said: O Sage, listen to this narrative which destroys all sins, pacifies every obstacle, and increases great spiritual welfare.
Then the god, the enemy of the asuras, having heard of his meeting with Śambhu, joyfully bestowed a reward upon the king of the twice-born.
Having praised the arrival of Śambhu, who was dear to Vārāṇasī, Hari then set out, placing Brahmā at his head.
Accompanied by Vivasvat and surrounded on all sides by those hosts, he was followed by the Yoginīs and stood near Gaṇeśa.
Then, having made the bull-bannered God of gods the guest of his eyes, the Lord of Śrī quickly descended from Tārkṣya and prostrated himself before him.
The grandfather too, being aged, with his neck deeply bowed, was prevented from prostrating by Mṛḍa himself, who had already been prostrated before him.
With his hand raised in a gesture of blessing, he consecrated him with the Rudra-hymns; then the Unborn One displayed unbroken grains that were moist and accompanied by fruits.
Having placed his crown at the lotus-feet of the Lord, Gaṇeśa bowed down quickly; Hara, out of joy, smelled the head of the elephant-faced one.
Having embraced him, he also seated him upon his own throne; then the Gaṇas, headed by Somanandi, prostrated themselves like a staff.
The Yoginīs also, having bowed to the Lord, sang auspicious songs; then Taraṇi prostrated before Hara, the lord of the Pramathas.
Then Khaṇḍenduśekhara, preceded by marks of honor, seated Hari upon the left side of his own throne.
Seeing Brahmā with a seat offered to him on the right side, all the hosts, honored by Śarva, bowed down.
Merely by the movement of his head, the yoginīs were propitiated; Ravi too was satisfied and entered [him] with a gesture of the hand.
Then Śatadhṛti, with his hands joined in a hollowed gesture of reverence, addressed Śambhu, whose lotus-like face was serene.
Brahmā said: O Blessed One, Lord of the gods, O Lord of Girijā, you must forgive me for the fact that, having reached Vārāṇasī, I did not return again.
O Moon-adorned One, who that has reached Kāśī—even if only by chance—would abandon it, even if he were capable of doing something else, while bearing the weight of old age? (22)
One cannot be deprived of one's brahminhood by its very nature; for if it were possible to deprive one of it, who would wish to perform meritorious deeds? (23)
Even for the powerful, this command must be understood as following the path of Dharma: no one who possesses knowledge should ever do anything harmful to anyone, anywhere. (24)
Who could harbor even the slightest hostile intent toward such a king, Divodāsa, the protector of Kāśī, who was untiring on the path of merit? (25)
Having heard these words, the exceedingly pure-minded Śrīkaṇṭha was pleased; smiling, he said to the Creator: "O Brahmā, I understand everything. (26)
The God of gods said: First, your status as a Brāhmaṇa was indeed faultless; furthermore, ten horse-sacrifices (vājimedha) were performed by you. (27)
Even more than that, O Brahmin, you have performed a supreme benefit for me by installing this Liṅga, despite my thousands of offenses. (28)
For him by whom even a single *liṅga* of mine has been installed anywhere, there is not even a trace of fault, despite his being guilty of all other offenses.
If one should offend a Brahmin even after a thousand offenses, his sovereignty will perish within just a few days.
While the Lord of Gods was speaking thus, the Gaṇas, along with their Mothers, looked all around at one another's faces and sighed inwardly.

The Sun, having perceived the opportune moment and beheld the beloved of Umā with a gracious countenance, bowed to Śambhu—the witness of all that has been seen, both moving and unmoving—and addressed him.
Arka said: "O Lord, having gone from here to Kāśī and performed service according to my ability, I have become powerless, despite possessing a thousand rays."
While that King Divodāsa, the protector of his own dharma, was ruling the earth, I remained here knowing that the arrival of Your Lordship was certain.
O Lord of Gods, awaiting your supreme audience and intent upon your worship, he divided himself into many forms.
Today the tree of my desires has borne fruit through the auspicious touch of your glance; watered by even a few drops of the water of devotion, it has blossomed through meditation. (36)
Having heard these words spoken by the Sun, the Three-eyed Lord, the Sovereign of the Gods, said: "O Bhāskara, you have committed no offense."
It is my own work that has been accomplished, since you have remained here while that king—who did not permit the entry of gods—was ruling. (38)
Having thus consoled Sūrya, the God of gods, that ocean of compassion, comforted the Gaṇas, whose necks were bowed low with shame.
Then the Yoginīs, having been clearly beheld by Śambhu and graced by him, departed with their necks bowed down as if overcome by a weight of shame. (40)
Then the three-eyed Lord directed his eyes toward the wielder of the discus; however, the high-minded Hari said nothing at all in the presence of the Omniscient One.
Lord Śiva, having heard the account from Tārkṣya regarding Gaṇeśa and Viṣṇu, became pleased in his mind alone and did not say anything at all.
In the meantime, five cows arrived from Goloka: Sunandā, Sumanā, Suśīlā, and likewise Surabhi. (43)
The fifth was Kapilā, who shatters the flood of all sins; through the compassionate glance of Bharga, their udders flowed [with milk].
The clouds rained down floods of milk from their udders with unceasing torrents until a lake was formed.
That second [ocean] was beheld by the attendants like the Ocean of Milk; through the presiding presence of the Lord of Gods, that became a supreme sacred site (tīrtha).
Maheśvara gave it the name Kapilāhrada; then, by the command of the God, all the inhabitants of heaven bathed there.
Then, from that sacred ford, the divine ancestors appeared; seeing them, all those gods joyfully offered libations to them.
The Agniṣvāttas, Barhiṣads, Ājyapas, and Somapas—these and other divine ancestors, being thus satisfied, addressed Śambhu. (49)
O God of gods, Lord of the universe, bestower of fearlessness upon devotees! By your presence at this sacred ford, an inexhaustible satisfaction has arisen within us.
"Therefore, O Śambhu, grant a boon with a gracious inner soul. Having heard these words of the divine ancestors, he whose banner is the bull [replied]: || 51 ||
While all the gods were listening, Śarva spoke these words, which provide supreme and ultimate satisfaction to all the ancestors.
The illustrious God of gods said: Listen, O Viṣṇu of mighty arms; listen also, O Grandfather, to this: in this Kāpila tīrtha, which is filled with the milk of Kapila’s son (Kāpileya). || 53 ||
"Those who shall offer funeral cakes (piṇḍas) with faith through the giving of śrāddha, for those ancestors there will be complete satisfaction by my command. (54)
I shall describe another supreme distinction that brings great satisfaction: a śrāddha offered here on the conjunction of the new moon (kuhū) and Monday is inexhaustible.
When the time of universal dissolution has arrived, even the waters of the mass of water perish; yet the Śrāddha performed at the conjunction of the Moon and the New Moon (Kuhū) does not perish here.
If a Śrāddha ceremony can be performed here at this Kapiladhāra Tīrtha during the conjunction of the new moon and a Monday, what need is there for Gayā or Puṣkara? (57)
"Where Gadādhara and Bhavānī are, O Grandfather, and where I am—the one whose banner is the bull—there Phalgu is present; of this there is no doubt. (58)
All the sacred fords (tīrthas) belonging to heaven, the atmosphere, and the earth shall dwell here on the new moon day joined with the lunar day of Soma.

Whatever merit is obtained from performing a śrāddha at Kurukṣetra, Naimiṣa, or at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean during an eclipse, that same merit is obtained at this tīrtha, O bull-bannered one.
I shall recount to you the names of this sacred ford, O divine Grandfathers, which are truly sufficient to grant you satisfaction.
This first lotus pond is known as Madhusravā; thereafter it should be understood as Kṛtakṛtyā, and then it becomes that ocean of milk.
